questions.question: Which Azure Storage service is designed for storing massive amounts of unstructured data, such as images, videos and backups?

options.why: Correct.
Queues store messages.
Tables store structured NoSQL key/attribute data.
Files provides SMB/NFS file shares.

questions.explanation: Blob Storage is object storage for unstructured data.

questions.scenario: A company wants to replace an on-premises file server with fully managed file shares that Windows clients can mount using SMB.
questions.question: Which service should it use?

options.why: Correct.
Archive is offline storage, not a mountable share.
Queues hold messages.
Cosmos DB is a database.

questions.explanation: Azure Files offers managed file shares accessible over SMB and NFS.

questions.question: Which Azure Storage service stores large numbers of messages so application components can communicate asynchronously?

options.why: Correct.
Disks are block storage for VMs.
Files are shares.
Tables store structured data.

questions.explanation: Queue Storage decouples components with messages.

questions.question: Which blob access tier is the cheapest for storage but keeps data offline and requires rehydration, which can take hours, before it can be read?

options.why: Correct.
Hot is for frequently accessed data and is online.
Cool is online, for infrequently accessed data.
Cold is online, for rarely accessed data.

questions.explanation: Archive has the lowest storage cost and highest access cost and latency. Data must be rehydrated first.

questions.scenario: Log files are accessed frequently for the first week, then rarely but must still be readable immediately for audit requests within 60 days.
questions.question: After the first week, which tier is the most appropriate?

options.why: Correct. It is online with lower storage cost for infrequently accessed data kept at least 30 days.
Archive data is not immediately readable.
Hot has higher storage cost for infrequent access.
That is VM disk storage, not a blob tier.

questions.explanation: Cool suits infrequently accessed data that must remain online. Lifecycle management can move blobs automatically.

questions.question: Which redundancy option keeps three copies of your data within a single datacenter in the primary region?

options.why: Correct.
ZRS spreads copies across three availability zones.
GRS also copies to a secondary region.
GZRS uses zones plus a secondary region.

questions.explanation: LRS is the cheapest option and protects against drive and rack failures, not a datacenter disaster.

questions.scenario: Data must survive the loss of an entire datacenter AND a full regional outage, and the primary copies should be spread across availability zones.
questions.question: Which redundancy option should you choose?

options.why: Correct. Zone redundancy in the primary region plus geo-replication.
LRS stays in one datacenter.
ZRS does not protect against a regional outage.
GRS uses LRS in the primary region, not zones.

questions.explanation: GZRS = ZRS in the primary region + LRS in the secondary region.

questions.question: What do RA-GRS and RA-GZRS add compared with GRS and GZRS?

options.text: Read access to the data in the secondary region at any time
options.why: Correct.

options.text: Write access in both regions at the same time
options.why: Writes go to the primary region.
Read-access geo options cost more.
Unrelated to redundancy.

questions.explanation: Read-access geo-redundancy lets applications read from the secondary endpoint even before a failover.

questions.question: Which statement about storage account names is true?

options.text: They must be globally unique across Azure
options.why: Correct. The name forms part of the public endpoint URL.

options.text: They must be unique only within a resource group
options.why: Uniqueness is global.

options.text: They can contain uppercase letters and spaces
options.why: Only lowercase letters and numbers, 3–24 characters.

options.text: They are generated randomly and cannot be chosen
options.why: You choose the name.

questions.explanation: Storage account names are 3–24 lowercase letters and numbers and must be unique across Azure.

questions.question: Which storage account type is recommended for most scenarios and supports blobs, files, queues and tables?

options.why: Correct.
Premium block blobs supports only block and append blobs.
This supports only file shares.
This supports only page blobs.

questions.explanation: Standard general-purpose v2 is the default choice for most workloads.

questions.question: Which command-line utility copies blobs or files to or from a storage account?

options.why: Correct.
File Sync synchronises Windows Server with Azure Files.
Data Box is a physical transfer device.
Advisor gives recommendations.

questions.explanation: AzCopy is a command-line tool for copying data to and from Azure Storage.

questions.scenario: A branch office wants to keep its Windows file server but cache frequently used files locally while storing everything centrally in Azure Files.
questions.question: Which service fits?

options.why: Correct. It syncs Windows Server with Azure Files and supports cloud tiering.
AzCopy copies data but does not continuously sync with caching.
Storage Explorer is a GUI management tool.
Migrate assesses and migrates workloads.

questions.explanation: Azure File Sync turns Windows Server into a fast cache of an Azure file share.

questions.scenario: A company must move 200 TB of data to Azure, but its internet connection would take months to upload it.
questions.question: What should it use?

options.why: Correct. A physical device is shipped, loaded and returned to Microsoft.
Unrelated.
Still limited by the same internet connection.
It transfers over the network.

questions.explanation: Data Box moves large data sets offline when network transfer is impractical.

questions.question: Which service provides a central hub to discover, assess and migrate on-premises servers, databases and web apps to Azure?

options.why: Correct.
Data Box transfers data offline.
Arc manages resources outside Azure; it is not a migration hub.
Purview governs data.

questions.explanation: Azure Migrate unifies discovery, assessment and migration tools.
